name: Model Monitoring
certifications: AWS Certified Machine Learning Engineer - Associate (MLA-C01)
Google Cloud Professional Machine Learning Engineer

beginner.summary: For analysts, data scientists and ML or DevOps engineers who have trained a model but have not yet run one in production. Covers why models fail silently, monitoring layers, prediction logging, service metrics with Prometheus, data quality checks, reference windows, drift tests (KS, chi-square, PSI), Evidently and whylogs reports, delayed labels and performance tracking, Grafana dashboards, basic alerting, batch jobs, false alarms, runbooks and a credit-scoring capstone.
prerequisites: Can train and score a model in Python with pandas and scikit-learn
Knows basic statistics: mean, standard deviation, distributions and p-values
Has Docker and Docker Compose installed and can run containers locally
outcomes: Instrument a model service and log predictions so that data, drift and performance can be monitored
Detect data quality faults and input drift with Pandera, Evidently, whylogs and statistical tests
Track performance when labels arrive late and show it on Grafana dashboards
Write tested alert rules and runbooks that turn a monitoring signal into a decision

intermediate.summary: For ML engineers and data scientists who already monitor a model with basic drift reports and want production-grade coverage. Covers concept drift detectors, multivariate drift, Alibi Detect, label-free performance estimation with NannyML, label pipelines, data contracts, slice and fairness monitoring, SHAP attribution tracking, scheduled monitoring at scale, alert engineering, SageMaker Model Monitor, Vertex AI, Azure ML and Databricks monitoring, challenger rollouts, skew detection and retraining triggers.
prerequisites: Completes the beginner path or runs at least one model with logged predictions and a drift report
Writes SQL and Python pipelines and has used Airflow or a similar scheduler
Knows Prometheus and Grafana basics and has access to one cloud ML platform
outcomes: Choose and combine univariate, multivariate and streaming detectors for covariate and concept drift
Estimate and track model performance despite delayed or partial labels
Monitor fairness, slices and attributions and operate managed monitors on SageMaker, Vertex AI, Azure ML or Databricks
Design alerts and retraining triggers that are tested, rate-limited and gated by evaluation

advanced.summary: For senior ML engineers, platform engineers and model risk leads who own monitoring for many models including LLM applications. Covers LLM tracing and quality monitoring, RAG, safety and agent monitoring, LLM drift and cost, streaming monitoring, statistical rigor, shift corrections, intersectional fairness, adversarial inputs, quality SLOs, governance and audit evidence, privacy-aware logging, fleet platform design, incident response, backtesting of monitors and a regulated capstone.
prerequisites: Operates at least one ML model and one LLM feature in production or a realistic replica
Comfortable with statistics for hypothesis testing and with Kafka or Spark basics
Has completed the intermediate path or equivalent experience with drift, labels and alerting
outcomes: Monitor LLM, RAG and agent systems for quality, safety, drift and cost
Apply rigorous statistics and backtesting to make monitors precise and trustworthy
Design a privacy-aware, config-driven monitoring platform for a large model fleet
Produce governance evidence and run incident response for regulated ML and LLM systems
